title: TrackFM: Far-out Compiler Support for a Far Memory World
problem: Large memory workloads require far memory systems extending the hierarchy across machines, but existing approaches present a fundamental tradeoff: kernel-based systems provide programmer transparency but sacrifice performance, while library-based systems achieve high performance but require programmer modifications. Current solutions cannot simultaneously achieve both efficiency and transparency.
motivation: Far memory systems can significantly improve application performance and cluster memory utilization for large workloads with favorable locality patterns.
method: TrackFM uses a compiler—the software that converts code to machine instructions—to figure out what data a program needs and where it should be stored across a network of computers (some memory on the local machine, some on remote machines). The compiler automatically inserts instructions to move data between local and remote memory while keeping copies consistent (a task called coherence), and a runtime system handles the actual data movement. Programs automatically get these far-memory capabilities after recompilation, without any code changes.
key_novelty: TrackFM's core idea is using the compiler to automatically manage memory across networked machines, solving the tradeoff where fast systems need programmer changes but simple systems are slow.
contributions: Design and implementation of TrackFM, a compiler-based far memory system
Outperforms kernel-based approaches by up to 2× while maintaining programmer transparency
Achieves performance within 10% of state-of-the-art library-based systems without requiring source code modifications
Transparent compilation model enabling far memory benefits through application recompilation only

metrics.speedup: up to 2× vs kernel-based, within 10% of library-based systems
